title: Voice Agent Adversarial Testing
summary: Adversarial test calls to your voice agent in English, Hindi and Hinglish: identity bypass, data disclosure, off-script promises and speech-layer flaws, with PASS, RISK and FAIL evidence.

seo.title: Voice Agent Adversarial Testing and Red-Teaming | VipraTech
seo.description: Synthetic adversarial callers test voice agents for identity bypass, data leakage, unsafe promises and speech-layer flaws in English, Hindi and Hinglish.

designed_for: Founder or CTO, Voice AI Company
CISO at a company deploying voice agents

problem.intro: Voice agents now verify callers, take payments, book appointments and handle complaints. They combine speech recognition, an LLM, text-to-speech and tool calls in real time, and each layer can fail in ways a text chatbot test will not catch. Callers also behave differently on the phone: they interrupt, switch languages and apply social pressure.

pain_points.title: Identity checks that can be talked around
pain_points.detail: Persistent or confused callers can sometimes get an agent to skip verification steps or accept partial answers.

pain_points.title: Disclosure to the wrong caller
pain_points.detail: Account details, appointment data or another customer's information can be read out when context or authentication is mishandled.

pain_points.title: Off-script commitments
pain_points.detail: Agents may promise refunds, waivers or outcomes that policy does not allow, especially under emotional pressure.

pain_points.title: Speech-layer surprises
pain_points.detail: Mis-transcribed words, code-switching, background noise and barge-in can change what the LLM believes the caller said.

solution.overview: We build and run adversarial test calls against your voice agent. Synthetic callers, driven by multi-turn playbooks and spoken through text-to-speech with different voices, accents and noise levels, call or stream into your agent the same way customers do. Playbooks cover verification bypass attempts, social engineering, requests for other customers' data, pressure to make unauthorised commitments, attempts to make the agent ignore its rules, abusive callers, switching between English, Hindi and Hinglish, and interruption patterns. Each call is recorded, transcribed and scored against your policy, then reviewed by a tester. Findings are graded PASS, RISK or FAIL and mapped to OWASP LLM and agentic risks, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF, with recordings as evidence.
capabilities: Multi-turn adversarial playbooks for verification bypass, social engineering and data disclosure
Synthetic callers with varied voices, accents, noise and interruption patterns
English, Hindi and Hinglish code-switching scenarios
Checks for unauthorised commitments and policy breaches
Tool-call checks where the agent books, takes payments or updates records
PASS, RISK and FAIL evidence with recordings, mapped to OWASP, MITRE ATLAS and NIST AI RMF

workflow.title: Capture the policy
workflow.detail: We record what the agent may and may not say or do: verification steps, disclosures, commitments and escalation rules.

workflow.title: Design playbooks
workflow.detail: Multi-turn adversarial playbooks are written for each risk area and language mix.

workflow.title: Place test calls
workflow.detail: Synthetic callers run the playbooks against a test number or streaming endpoint.

workflow.title: Score the calls
workflow.detail: Audio, transcripts and tool calls are scored against the policy automatically.

workflow.title: Tester review
workflow.detail: A tester listens to RISK and FAIL calls, confirms findings and rates severity.

workflow.title: Report and retest
workflow.detail: You receive evidence and fixes, and failed playbooks are rerun after changes.

inputs: Test phone number or streaming endpoint for the voice agent

human_in_the_loop: A tester listens to every RISK and FAIL call before it becomes a finding, because tone, timing and partial disclosures are hard to judge from a transcript alone. Your team decides on fixes and release timing.

faqs.q: Do you test in Hindi and Hinglish?
faqs.a: Yes. Playbooks run in English, Hindi and Hinglish, including mid-sentence switching, which is where many voice agents behave differently. Other Indian languages can be added with native-speaker review.

faqs.q: Can you test a voice agent built on a third-party platform?
faqs.a: Yes. We call a test number or connect to the streaming endpoint, so the platform does not matter. Tool-call logs from the platform make findings more precise.

faqs.q: How is this different from QA testing?
faqs.a: QA checks that the agent does what it should for normal callers. Adversarial testing checks what it does when a caller is trying to make it fail, mislead it or extract data.

faqs.q: Do real customers ever hear the test calls?
faqs.a: No. Tests run only against test numbers or endpoints and staging data you provide.
